title: Passing things on instead of binning them
description: A clear-out feels better and wastes less when unwanted things go to people who actually want them.

body.heading: One household's clutter is another's find
paragraphs: The outgrown bike, the duplicate toaster and the box of paperbacks are only rubbish if they reach the bin. Listed on a local giving group, offered to a charity shop or put out with a friendly free sign, the same items often find a new home within days.
Passing things on also beats storing them for a someday that never comes. The cupboard space you get back is its own reward.

body.heading: Make it easy for the next owner
paragraphs: Clean items, honest descriptions and a clear photo make the difference between a quick collection and a listing that lingers. Mention faults plainly; people happily take a scratched table for a workshop that they would feel cheated by if surprised.
Bundle small things together: a bag of children's clothes in one size, a box of kitchen bits. Bundles move faster and save everyone multiple trips.

body.heading: A swap shelf, a swap evening
paragraphs: Some streets and workplaces keep an informal swap shelf where books, plants and puzzles circulate. Among friends, a clothes or toy swap evening turns decluttering into a social event, with everyone's leftovers becoming someone else's novelty.
What cannot be given away can often be recycled, and what can be neither is a much smaller pile than the one you started with. That is the quiet mathematics of passing things on.

takeaway: Clean it, describe it honestly and offer it locally first, and most clutter becomes someone else's useful find.
